# Independent audit: exposed complete bases in the smooth singleton problem

Audited `candidate cf5052b52df57b8d` in full. The stated theorem and its limitation pass.

1. At an exposed vertex p of the COMPLETE finite base hull, a single affine gap g is strictly positive at every other sampled base. The tangent-line extension J is finite convex and nonnegative on the whole real line and equals s^(-d) on the full own-fiber range of the positive projective normalizer. The own support height h_y(n) is positive and continuous on the unit normal sphere. Compactness therefore gives one finite T uniformly in the normal, making [h_y J(P_y)-Tg]_+ vanish on every other sampled boundary. This is an actual normal-dependent physical convex field, without any limiting localization.

2. The projective cone weight is exactly h_y/P_y^d. In ordinary coordinates,

       div((x-y)/P_y(x)^d)=d/P_y(x)^(d+1).

   For a through-y halfspace the extra flat boundary has zero radial flux. Thus both the full boundary mass and the through-y cap mass equal d times the corresponding projective-image volume. The projective image has centroid zero by the attained energy stationarity, so the ordinary sharp Grünbaum factor gives the exact own-source credit. Outward smoothing and the nonnegative H buffer only increase the captured profile on this own through-y side.

3. Normalize each isolated field to surface integral one. Their sum has integral k, and each source profile receives its own credit Gamma_d plus nonnegative cross credits. The argument works with the actual within-source separator weights, regardless of whether those are the original covering weights rho. After normalizing each nonzero source mixture, the global capture weights sum to one. Testing the actual positive smooth stress consequently gives B_*>=Gamma_d/k. No independent per-source separator or unproved source-volume row is used.

4. Being a vertex of the DEEPEST-base hull does not supply the affine gap on the COMPLETE base. The note makes this distinction correctly; it does not close the interior-source case by parity.

5. The simplex product example checks the obstruction to using the unlocalized constant chart. A finite exposing base tilt makes all other smoothed fiber contributions exactly zero because the kernel has compact transition support. On the selected own fiber, integration by parts gives the displayed dQ plus slab-moment term, whose sign is nonpositive. The denominator has the exact extra factor 2^n. The source is the simplex centroid by affine simplex symmetry and uniqueness in its own fiber, and P_y=1 by energy stationarity. Hence the claimed failure of individual Gamma_d efficiency for the unlocalized chart occurs within the actual smoothed source geometry. This example is not asserted to be a global smooth body minimum.

The boundary and d=1 conventions are consistent: facet measure is counting measure in d=1, the own height is positive, and the same divergence/cone identity applies. No correction is needed. The unresolved issue is precisely extending the source payment to source bases that are not exposed vertices of the complete base hull.
